text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN`. With no parseable digits, `parseInt(str, 10)` is `NaN`, so it falls into the fallback loop, which builds an empty string `""` (no hanidec chars, no code points in any of the `numberingSystemsUTF16` ranges), and `parseInt("", 10)` is `NaN`.
It returns `[matches, {}]`, where `matches` is `null` (the result of `input.match(regex)` when there is no match). So effectively `[null, {}]` — a null match plus an empty object of parsed values.

Fixed. In `Interval.fromISO` (src/interval.js), `DateTime.fromISO` was called directly, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid` set it threw an `InvalidDateTimeError` for the duration half of `P1Y/2016-01-01` (and `2016-01-01/P1Y`) before the Duration fallback could run. Both endpoint parses are now wrapped in try/catch, recording validity instead of propagating the throw, so duration-based intervals still parse and genuinely unparsable input still throws `InvalidIntervalError`. Also fixed the "asISO 8601" typo in the invalid explanation. Verified: `Interval.fromISO("P1Y/2016-01-01")`, `"2016-01-01/P1Y"`, `"2016-01-01/2016-12-31"` no longer throw while `"blah/blah"` does; all 9 interval test suites (127 tests) pass, and the full suite shows the same 2 pre-existing failures (French locale formatting in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js) as before my change.

It returns `unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)` — i.e. an `Invalid` object (truthy) with reason `"unit out of range"` and explanation `"you specified <value> as a weekYear, which is invalid"`. Because `validYear = isInteger(obj.weekYear)` is false, the `!validYear` branch is taken first, so the week/weekday checks never run (the `weeksInWeekYear` call in the next line is still evaluated but doesn't throw).
It returns `LocalZone.instance` — the getter is `return defaultZone || LocalZone.instance;`, so a null internal `defaultZone` falls back to the local zone singleton.

It returns the string `"[error]"` (after `console.error(e)`), because the `catch` block returns early before the `switch` that would otherwise format the result.

`latn` (i.e. `\d`). The signature is `digitRegex({ numberingSystem }, append = "")` and the body is `new RegExp(`${numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]}${append}`)` — when `numberingSystem` is undefined/null/empty it falls back to the `latn` entry, which is the regex `\d`.

#1 done (fixed & verified). #4 done (fixed & verified: `objToLocalTS` now re-sets month/day via `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`; all day-arithmetic across the 0–99/100 boundary now matches proleptic Gregorian). #8 done (fixed & verified: `isInDST` now compares against `set({ month: 1, day: 1 })`, so the 1974 US year-round DST window reports true). #11 is in progress — I've reproduced it (`Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}).normalize()` yields NaN because the conversion matrix lacks quarters→seconds); ETA ~5 minutes.

It sets the internal `defaultZone` to `null` (`if (!z) { defaultZone = null; }`), i.e. it clears the default zone so the getter falls back to `LocalZone.instance`. A non-falsy value is instead passed through `normalizeZone(z)`.

It's an abstract getter: it throws a `ZoneIsAbstractError` (`throw new ZoneIsAbstractError();`) rather than returning anything. It exists only to declare the interface, so concrete subclasses (LocalZone, IANAZone, FixedOffsetZone, InvalidZone) must override it to return their type string.

Fixed. `objToLocalTS` (src/impl/util.js) reverted the legacy 19XX year mapping with `setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which kept the day-overflow arithmetic done in the 19xx year (2000 is a leap year, 100 is not), so day math that crossed February of year 100 was off by a day (e.g. 0099-12-31 + 61 days gave 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02). It now re-sets year, month and day together: `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`. Verified against a proleptic-Gregorian reference for every day offset from -400 to +800 across 12 start dates spanning years 0–1900: 0 mismatches. Full suite unchanged apart from the 2 pre-existing failures.

Fixed. `DateTime#isInDST` compared `this.offset` against `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset`, which is the same instant (hence the same offset) whenever the DateTime is already in January — so the 1974 US year-round DST period (Jan 6 – Oct 27) reported false. It now compares against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset` (Jan 1 is always standard time in the US), so every instant in that window reports true. Verified: for all of 1974 in America/New_York, `isInDST` now exactly matches "offset === -240"; 1974-01-05 and 1974-10-28 report false; the existing pre-DST/during-DST/post-DST tests still pass.

Fixed. The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing entries: `years.quarters` (both the casual and accurate matrices) and `quarters.seconds` (casual matrix). Because `convert()` looks up `matrix[toUnit][fromUnit]`, those lookups returned `undefined`, so `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize()` (and `{ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }`) produced NaN values. Added `quarters: 4` to both `years` maps and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to the casual `quarters` map. Verified: all 72 ordered unit pairs now normalize without NaN, `as()`/`shiftTo()` are NaN-free for every pair, and normalized totals still match the pre-normalization totals in milliseconds. Existing duration tests all pass.

Fixed. `padStart` (src/impl/util.js) prepended zeros and then sliced the last n characters, so negative numbers lost their sign's digit: `padStart(-10, 4)` returned "0-10" and `padStart(-1, 4)` returned "00-1", making `toISODate()`/`toISO()` emit e.g. "0-10-05-25" for year -10. It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign: `"-" + ("" + -input).padStart(n, "0")`. Verified: years -1, -10, -100 now render as "-0001-05-25", "-0010-05-25", "-0100-05-25" (and positive years are unchanged).

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from the parsed offset: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (the `Z` token's value is the offset in minutes, already deserialized by the token handler). That zone is returned as the second element of the `[vals, zone]` pair. The `z` (IANA name) branch is only used when `matches.Z` is undefined, and `null` if neither is present.

Fixed. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `return true`, so `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` (or `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")`) claimed to be valid. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` (importing `isNumber` from impl/util.js), so a non-numeric offset makes the zone invalid; `DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone})` yields an invalid DateTime and `DateTime.fromObject({year: 2017, zone})` now returns an invalid DateTime with reason "unsupported zone" instead of silently producing a bogus DateTime. Valid numeric offsets (including the UTC singleton and `FixedOffsetZone.instance(60)`) are unaffected, and the full suite still shows only the 2 pre-existing failures.

Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly zero: `hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` (the `validHour` check is `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)`). So 24:00:00.000 is accepted (as end-of-day) while e.g. 24:00:01 or 24:30 is rejected with a "hour" unit-out-of-range error.
